text:
Vegas signed Marc Gatcomb on July 1 to bring hits to the fourth line, and on that count he has delivered: 74 in 21 games, at about 10 and a half minutes a night. The undrafted forward from Woburn, Massachusetts, who came over from the Islanders as a free agent, plays the energy role the Golden Knights wanted to fill.

Everything else has been a struggle. He has two points all season and none in his last 18 games, and unlike some droughts, this one is not just bad luck: the chances have thinned out too, and he has one goal on 29 shots. The bigger worry is what happens when he is on the ice. At five on five Vegas has taken just 36% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, about 20 points worse than without him, and his minutes have slipped by more than a minute a night over the last ten games. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him taking chances away from opponents better than 91% of forwards, though in under 500 minutes. That defensive version is what earned him the contract, and it is the one Vegas has not seen yet.
headline: Marc Gatcomb brings the hits, but the ice tilts away
